item.content:encoded:
UAE dealer Gargash Prime Automotive has opened preorders for Xiaomi’s SU7 electric sedan, YU7 electric SUV and SkyNomad range-extended SUV. Prices start at AED 169,900 for the SU7, AED 184,900 for the YU7 and AED 209,900 for the SkyNomad. The dealer lists December 2026 availability for initial versions.

The sales channel also offers leasing and local after-sales packages, including warranties of up to five years or 150,000 kilometers and maintenance coverage of up to 60,000 kilometers. Additional variants are listed for February 2027 delivery. The listings give UAE buyers a local purchase and service channel as Xiaomi prepares its broader overseas automotive expansion. [ChinaEVHome]

item.content:encoded:
Huawei disclosed details of the Kirin 9050 series’ security architecture on Wednesday, saying the mobile chips support post-quantum cryptography and have undergone testing for resistance to quantum attacks. The architecture combines a mobile security processor with an embedded secure-element chip and has received CCRC EAL5+ security certification, according to Huawei.

The two security components work together to support secure boot, data protection, privacy and communications security. Post-quantum cryptography is designed to protect information against future quantum computers that could compromise widely used encryption methods. The disclosure follows Huawei’s recent technical breakdowns of the Kirin 9050’s computing, imaging and display capabilities. [IT Home, in Chinese]

Musk, who was visiting the city for APEC-related events, also described himself as a “super fan” of China. Tesla’s Shanghai factory is central […]
item.content:encoded:
Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the company would continue increasing production in China during a meeting with China Council for the Promotion of International Trade Chairman Ren Hongbin in Shenzhen on Thursday. Musk, who was visiting the city for APEC-related events, also described himself as a “super fan” of China.

Tesla’s Shanghai factory is central to its global manufacturing and export network. It produces the Model 3 and Model Y for buyers in China and overseas, making any further increase in output relevant to both markets. Musk’s remarks signal continued commitment to Chinese production, although he provided no timetable or volume target. [IT Home, in Chinese]

item.content:encoded:
Huawei announced the Watch Air on Thursday, describing the 6.9 mm device as its thinnest smartwatch. It will debut at the company’s November 24 product event alongside the Mate X8 foldable and Mate 90 Air smartphone.

Leaker Digital Chat Station expects the watch to feature a 1.92-inch rectangular AMOLED display, narrow bezels and a titanium body weighing 27 grams. The leaker also claims it will offer around a week of battery life, with health features comparable to Huawei’s Watch 6 and sports functions aligned with the GT 7 Pro. Huawei has yet to announce pricing or confirm the complete specifications. [IT Home, in Chinese]

item.content:encoded:
Tencent released the weights for its Hy4 flash AI model on Wednesday, two days after launching it through its apps and cloud API. Developers can download the standard model, an FP8 version and a base model for further training. The release makes good on Tencent’s announcement that it planned to make the model’s weights available.

Hy4 flash supports text and image inputs and a context window of up to one million tokens. It has approximately 224 billion parameters, with around 12 billion activated per token, and targets everyday productivity tasks such as research, document preparation and spreadsheet work. Tencent has published deployment materials alongside the weights under its Tencent Hy License. [Tencent]

item.content:encoded:
Huawei announced the Mate 90 Air on Thursday, adding a slim handset to its flagship smartphone family. The phone will debut at the company’s November 24 event alongside the Mate X8 foldable. Huawei’s online store lists rose gold, silver and black versions, with 12 GB of RAM and either 256 GB or 512 GB of storage.

Full-payment preorders are scheduled to open at 6:08 p.m. Beijing time on launch day. Huawei has yet to disclose the price or complete specifications. Leaker Digital Chat Station expects a seven-inch display, a body measuring between six and seven millimeters thick, three rear cameras and 66-watt charging. [IT Home, in Chinese]

item.title: Meituan brings cable-lowering delivery drones to Dubai
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Meituan unveiled its M-Drone 4L delivery drone in Dubai on Wednesday, marking the model’s first overseas appearance. The aircraft hovers above a delivery point and lowers packages by cable. Meituan said routes using the new drone would begin operating shortly in locations including the Sobha Hartland residential community and outdoor spaces. The system selects a […]
item.content:encoded:
Meituan unveiled its M-Drone 4L delivery drone in Dubai on Wednesday, marking the model’s first overseas appearance. The aircraft hovers above a delivery point and lowers packages by cable. Meituan said routes using the new drone would begin operating shortly in locations including the Sobha Hartland residential community and outdoor spaces.

The system selects a drop-off point and suppresses package swinging during descent, then uses force sensors and an electronically controlled hook to release the load. Meituan says it has tested the drone in temperatures from minus 20°C to 50°C, heavy rain and Dubai’s dusty conditions. The company has operated delivery routes in Dubai since receiving a commercial beyond-visual-line-of-sight permit in December 2024. The new model is intended to extend service from collection lockers to locations closer to customers’ homes. [Meituan, in Chinese]

item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: DeepSeek has removed separate charges for web searches, image searches and webpage fetching performed through its models’ built-in server-side tools. Developers now pay for the model tokens used during those interactions, including the material retrieved and processed. The change took effect on November 18. The tools let developers build applications that search for current information […]
item.content:encoded:
DeepSeek has removed separate charges for web searches, image searches and webpage fetching performed through its models’ built-in server-side tools. Developers now pay for the model tokens used during those interactions, including the material retrieved and processed. The change took effect on November 18.

The tools let developers build applications that search for current information and read webpages as part of a model conversation. The pricing change applies when the model invokes those tools. Applications that call the standalone Search and Fetch APIs directly continue to pay the corresponding request fees. [DeepSeek, in Chinese]

item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Tencent has substantially reduced spending on its Yuanbao AI app after it failed to achieve the success the company initially expected, President Martin Lau said on Wednesday. Speaking on Tencent’s earnings call, Lau said Yuanbao’s focus had shifted from expanding its user base to improving its capabilities. Its recently launched AI search service is also […]
item.content:encoded:
Tencent has substantially reduced spending on its Yuanbao AI app after it failed to achieve the success the company initially expected, President Martin Lau said on Wednesday. Speaking on Tencent’s earnings call, Lau said Yuanbao’s focus had shifted from expanding its user base to improving its capabilities. Its recently launched AI search service is also available to other businesses.

The adjustment comes as Tencent develops several AI products with different roles. Yuanbao serves consumers seeking information and advice, while WorkBuddy handles workplace tasks and WeChat’s Xiaowei assistant operates within the messaging platform. Lau said Tencent would continue evaluating whether its AI investments produce useful products, with usage expected to develop into revenue and eventually profit. [National Business Daily, in Chinese]

item.title: Can RayNeo’s smart glasses become a habit?
item.dc:creator: Lucia
item.description: Editor’s note: Founded in 2021 and incubated by TCL Electronics, RayNeo makes AR and smart glasses for entertainment, productivity and AI assistance. IDC ranked it second globally in AR/VR headset shipments in Q2 2026, with a 12% share. Its backers include early investors Fosun Capital and Winreal Investment, as well as China Mobile-linked funds and […]
item.content:encoded:
Editor’s note: Founded in 2021 and incubated by TCL Electronics, RayNeo makes AR and smart glasses for entertainment, productivity and AI assistance. IDC ranked it second globally in AR/VR headset shipments in Q2 2026, with a 12% share. Its backers include early investors Fosun Capital and Winreal Investment, as well as China Mobile-linked funds and CITIC Goldstone, with a China Unicom-affiliated fund participating in a D round exceeding RMB 1 billion in January 2026. The question now is whether RayNeo can turn its market traction into glasses people reach for every day.

A long flight, a hotel room or a wait between appointments can leave people looking for a bigger screen — or a way to check information without pulling out a phone. RayNeo’s latest lineup takes two different approaches: the minimalist iO, built around a small information display, and the maximalist GT series, which turns connected devices into a large virtual screen.

Two Ways to Wear a Screen

Launched internationally at IFA in September, the iO is designed to look like ordinary eyewear. At about 33 grams, it uses a small monochrome heads-up display for captions, live translation and prompts. Voice capture and AI features add meeting notes and reminders. The pitch is a light-touch assistant that can stay on throughout the day.

That puts iO in a different lane from camera-led glasses such as Meta’s Ray-Ban line. As Wareable noted, RayNeo is not positioning it as a direct rival to Meta’s camera glasses, but as a lightweight ambient assistant built around a small display and voice interaction.

The GT series takes the opposite approach. Designed for movies, games and work, the glasses connect to another device to create a large virtual screen. The GT Max can expand it to the equivalent of 307 inches, with spatial tracking and audio tuned by Bang & Olufsen. It is closer to a personal theater than an all-purpose computer.

A Tom’s Guide hands-on praised the GT Max’s comfort, while describing this category more accurately as “display glasses” — a wearable screen, not a self-contained AR computer. The GT’s job is to make a connected phone, laptop or console more immersive, not replace it.

The Bigger AR Ambition

RayNeo’s longer-term goal is more ambitious. Its X3 Pro, a standalone AI+AR model, weighs 76 grams and combines binocular full-color MicroLED displays with cameras, navigation, translation and AI. A TechRadar review praised its display but flagged its 245mAh battery and high price as major trade-offs.

Founder and CEO Li Hongwei has also pushed back the timeline for the category’s breakthrough. In a 2026 iFanr interview, he said AI had advanced faster than expected, while optical displays, chips and spatial computing had moved more slowly. His “iPhone moment” forecast has shifted from around 2025 to 2027.

Money for a Longer Race

Founded in 2021 and incubated by TCL Electronics, RayNeo has raised capital across multiple rounds. Its first external round, an A round of more than RMB 100 million in 2023, was led by Fosun Capital and Winreal Investment. Bilibili and Huatai Zijin later joined its investor base.

In January 2026, RayNeo raised more than RMB 1 billion in a D round co-led by China Mobile’s investment arm and CITIC Goldstone Investment, with a China Unicom-affiliated fund participating. D+ and D++ rounds followed in May and October, with amounts undisclosed.

Telecom backing could matter if glasses become independent connected devices: eSIM services, networks and distribution may prove as important as optics.

RayNeo has market momentum. Omdia ranked it second in global XR headwear shipments in the first half of 2026, with a 9.9% share. IDC later put it second in the broader AR/VR headset market in Q2, with 12%, and first in extended-reality glasses, with 25.2%. Meta led that broader market with 45.7%, according to IDC.

For now, RayNeo is pursuing two habits: wearing glasses for quick information throughout the day and putting them on for a big screen when there is time to sit back. Whether either becomes routine will matter more than how futuristic the hardware looks.
